fixture.expectedBug: window.py accepts the excluded end boundary

summary.purpose: Changes the end comparison in window.contains. The repository contract, README and test say windows are half-open [start, end), so the end must be excluded.

commits.explanation: Replaces `value < end` with `value <= end` in contains, so the end boundary is now accepted. This reverses the previous commit's half-open behavior and contradicts the README contract and test_window_end.

findings.title: contains accepts the window end, breaking the half-open contract
findings.body:
`value <= end` makes `contains(10, 20, 20)` return True. The README defines windows as `[start, end)` and requires that adjacent windows never both accept a shared boundary. With this change, `contains(10, 20, 20)` and `contains(20, 30, 20)` are both True, and `test_window_end` fails.

```suggestion
    return start <= value < end
```
evidenceExplanations:
At head a8cd427, `python3 -B test_contract.py` exits 1 with `AssertionError: True is not false : END_EXCLUSIVE`. Adjacent windows [10,20) and [20,30) both accept 20 (True True). The previous commit's window.py returns False for contains(10,20,20).

Validation: Reproduced at the frozen head. The failing test and the adjacent-window check both violate the documented contract, and the previous commit (99dac51) behaves correctly. I found no guard, override or other owner that would make `<=` intentional; the PR body says only 'Adjust the end comparison'.

README.md states 'Windows include their start and exclude their end: [start, end)' and 'Adjacent windows must not both accept their shared boundary.' test_contract.py asserts contains(10, 20, 20) is False.

summary.purpose: Changes the window containment check in window.py. The repository contract is half-open windows [start, end), so the end must be excluded.

commits.explanation: Changes contains() from `start <= value < end` to `start <= value <= end`, which makes the end boundary inclusive. This reverses the previous half-open behavior and contradicts the README and the END_EXCLUSIVE test assertion.

findings.title: contains() makes the window end inclusive, breaking the half-open contract
findings.body:
`start <= value <= end` accepts `end`, but windows are documented as `[start, end)`. `contains(10, 20, 20)` now returns True, so adjacent windows such as `[10, 20)` and `[20, 30)` both accept 20, and the existing `END_EXCLUSIVE` test fails.

```suggestion
    return start <= value < end
```
evidenceExplanations:
Head window.py line 2 is `return start <= value <= end`.

Validation: Reproduced at the frozen head: the suite fails on the END_EXCLUSIVE assertion and the adjacent-window check shows a double-accepted boundary. With the base one-line version and identical test files, the suite passes. The README states the half-open contract, so the change is a regression, not intended behavior. Only the `<` to `<=` edit differs. I ran the control from a copy in $TMPDIR and left the worktree unchanged.
